question: Using determinants, find the equation of the line through $(2,3)$ and $(5,9)$. If $(k,7)$ lies on this line, determine $k$ and justify the result.
explanation:
Formation of the determinant
For an arbitrary point $(x,y)$ on the line, $$\begin{vmatrix}x&y&1\\2&3&1\\5&9&1\end{vmatrix}=0$$
Expansion and simplification
Expanding gives $$x(3-9)-y(2-5)+(18-15)=0$$ Therefore, $$-6x+3y+3=0$$ Dividing by $3$, $$2x-y-1=0$$
Application of the point condition
Since $(k,7)$ lies on the line, $$2k-7-1=0$$
Determination and verification
Thus, $2k=8$ and $k=4$. The point $(4,7)$ satisfies $2(4)-7-1=0$, verifying the result.
